notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver, but the upstream builds every request from parts (IN_PV_S<channel>, OUT_SP_<on|off><channel> <value> mbar, REMOTE 1, OUT_VENT 0), so this package is a direct Driver with native.py; the card's decision is already direct-driver. The gate was run on the fake backend only. native.py and the real connio/DCP3000 path were never run and no hardware was attached; the fake is an in-memory stand-in with values marked placeholder from the upstream sinstruments simulator, not a recording. No page of docs/dcp_3000.pdf was read, so no PDF page is cited. The event interval and the eight on/off set points are Limit.operator_required: no text file of the clone states their ranges, and every write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site supplies them. site-limits.example.json is an example, not a statement about any unit. recording_time_interval is read-only because the upstream async setter calls self.write(...) without awaiting the coroutine (vacuubrand/dcp3000/dcp3000.py:46-50), so its write would never reach the device. The pressure read and cap.measure.pressure.v1 publish Pa: upstream decode_pressure converts Torr to mbar and hPa is numerically equal to mbar. NOT COVERED: the recording interval write (broken upstream on asyncio) and a configuration write (the clone has only IN_CFG). The pump state is not observable in the clone, so the safe state only claims the commands REMOTE - and OUT_VENT 0, not a pump stop. Risk R1; no independent hardware e-stop is cited and none is claimed. The package is model-authored, reviewed_by is null, and no human review or hardware run is claimed; the loader's unreviewed-hardware refusal applies only at R2 and R3, so this R1 package does not rely on it.
